# TildaZ v0.9.2

**Alt combinations now reach the program running inside TildaZ.**

- `Alt+n` works in zellij, tmux and emacs. Until now the Alt key was dropped, so
  `Alt+a` arrived as a plain `a`.
  ([#533](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/533))
- Arrow and function keys carry their modifiers too — `Shift+Left` and `Alt+Left` now
  send `CSI 1;2D` and `CSI 1;3D`, where before they sent nothing at all.
- On macOS, `[input] macos_option_as_alt` chooses whether Option types characters
  (`option+a` → `å`, the default) or acts as Alt.

## Upgrade notes

**Your `config_N.toml` needs a new `[input]` section.** The schema is checked in both
directions, so a config written by an older version stops the app with
`missing required key "macos_option_as_alt"`. Add this by hand, or move the file aside
and let TildaZ write a fresh one:

```toml
[input]
macos_option_as_alt = "none"   # none | both | left | right
```

The key exists on all three platforms so one config file stays portable between them,
but it only does something on macOS — on Linux and Windows Alt is always Meta, because
`Alt+a` produces no character there.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Linux portable (glibc 2.28+) | `tildaz-v0.9.2-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.tar.gz` | Extract and run `./install.sh`; no `sudo`. |
| Linux Debian / Ubuntu | `tildaz_0.9.2-1_{amd64,arm64}.deb` | Install with `dpkg` or a graphical software installer. |
| Linux Fedora / RHEL / openSUSE | `tildaz-0.9.2-1.{x86_64,aarch64}.rpm` | Install with `dnf` or the distro package tool. |
| Linux distro-independent | `TildaZ-0.9.2-{x86_64,aarch64}.AppImage` | Make executable and run; FUSE is optional. |
| Arch / Manjaro / EndeavourOS | `tildaz-0.9.2-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst` | x86_64 package. |
| macOS 14+ universal | `tildaz-v0.9.2-macos.dmg` | Apple Silicon and Intel; stable self-signed identity, not notarized. |
| Windows 10/11 x64 | `tildaz-v0.9.2-win-x64.zip` | Unzip and keep `_internal\` next to `tildaz.exe`. |
| Windows 11 ARM64 | `tildaz-v0.9.2-win-arm64.zip` | ARM64-native binary; same layout as the x64 zip. |
